answer: Drifting Wharf Ledger.** Each identity must answer a fresh, timing-sensitive challenge routed through a rotating wharf node, and answers are signed with a locally trained zephyr seed. Duplicate agents sharing one seed produce correlated timing fingerprints, which the ledger flags as a marble-like trace and quarantines. An attacker cloning N identities must train and host N distinct seeds, paying full compute and latency cost per clone rather than reusing one.
